tasks.title: Scripted, pinned, non-Nix install of the GHC WebAssembly toolchain
tasks.prompt:
You are implementing one task of milestone M0 of the SXC-1 Trainer project.
Repository root: /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1 (a git repo; there is no GitHub remote yet).
Project context: the site is a Haskell/Miso application compiled to WebAssembly and served
as static files. This task installs the compiler toolchain. You own exactly ONE file:

    /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/install-toolchain.sh

Do not create or edit any other file in the repository. Other agents own the rest.

PINNED VERSIONS FOR MILESTONE M0 (do not substitute):
  ghc-wasm-meta   github.com/haskell-wasm/ghc-wasm-meta @ c75985a1b58fb0376eea9149ba5c7b933b3c7455
  GHC wasm        FLAVOUR=9.14   (base 4.22.0.0, template-haskell 2.24.0.0, text 2.1.3,
                                  bytestring 0.12.2.0, containers 0.8, mtl 2.3.1,
                                  transformers 0.6.1.2, ghc-experimental 9.1401.0)
  miso            1.12.0.0 from Hackage, with index-state 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z
  WASI shim       @bjorn3/browser_wasi_shim 0.3.0
  toolchain root  $HOME/.ghc-wasm  (env script: $HOME/.ghc-wasm/env)

BACKGROUND YOU MUST NOT REDISCOVER THE HARD WAY
The upstream-documented install is
    curl https://gitlab.haskell.org/haskell-wasm/ghc-wasm-meta/-/raw/master/bootstrap.sh | sh
DO NOT USE IT. gitlab.haskell.org is behind an "Anubis" proof-of-work anti-bot wall: from
this machine that URL returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type text/html -- an HTML challenge
page -- for both a curl user-agent and a spoofed browser user-agent. Piping it to sh would
execute a web page. The `-/archive/master.tar.gz` endpoint is walled the same way.
Use the GitHub read-only mirror instead and let git verify integrity by commit hash.
All actual binary distributions referenced by ghc-wasm-meta live on GitHub Releases
(github.com/haskell-wasm/*) and downloads.haskell.org, both of which ARE reachable.

WHAT THE SCRIPT MUST DO
1. `#!/usr/bin/env bash`, `set -euo pipefail`. Support `--help`, `--check`, `--force`.
   Resolve the repo root from BASH_SOURCE so it works from any cwd.
2. Constants at the top, clearly named and commented:
       GHC_WASM_META_URL=https://github.com/haskell-wasm/ghc-wasm-meta.git
       GHC_WASM_META_COMMIT=c75985a1b58fb0376eea9149ba5c7b933b3c7455
       FLAVOUR=9.14
       PREFIX="${GHC_WASM_PREFIX:-$HOME/.ghc-wasm}"
3. Preflight: verify these commands exist and fail with one clear message listing anything
   missing -- git curl tar xz unzip unzstd jq make cc sed realpath. Verify at least 12 GiB
   free on the filesystem holding $PREFIX. (All of these are present on this machine; the
   check is for fresh clones elsewhere.)
4. `--check` mode: run preflight, then report whether a working install exists -- i.e.
   $PREFIX/env is readable AND $PREFIX/wasm32-wasi-ghc/bin/wasm32-wasi-ghc
   --numeric-version succeeds. Print the GHC version and the recorded pin. Exit 0 if
   installed and healthy, non-zero otherwise. Perform no downloads in this mode.
5. Normal mode: if `--check` would have succeeded and `--force` was not given, print
   "toolchain already installed (use --force to reinstall)" and exit 0. This makes the
   script idempotent and keeps CI cache hits cheap.
6. Install:
       tmp=$(mktemp -d); trap cleanup EXIT
       git clone "$GHC_WASM_META_URL" "$tmp/ghc-wasm-meta"
       git -C "$tmp/ghc-wasm-meta" checkout --detach "$GHC_WASM_META_COMMIT"
       # assert `git -C ... rev-parse HEAD` equals the pin, abort if not
       FLAVOUR=9.14 PREFIX="$PREFIX" bash "$tmp/ghc-wasm-meta/setup.sh"
   NOTE: ghc-wasm-meta's setup.sh begins with `rm -rf "$PREFIX"`. That is expected; warn
   the user before doing it when --force was used.
7. After setup.sh, in a subshell: source "$PREFIX/env" and print
   `wasm32-wasi-ghc --numeric-version`, `wasm32-wasi-cabal --version | head -1`, and
   whether `wasm-opt` and `wasm-tools` resolved on PATH. Fail the script if
   wasm32-wasi-ghc or wasm32-wasi-cabal is missing.
8. Write a stamp file "$PREFIX/.sxc1-toolchain-stamp" containing the pinned commit, the
   flavour, the resolved GHC version and an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp, one `key=value` per
   line. `--check` reads and prints it.
9. Finish by printing the next command the user should run:
   `./scripts/build-site.sh`, and the reminder to `source $PREFIX/env` for manual work.
10. Never pipe a download into a shell anywhere in this file.
11. `chmod +x` the script.

HOW TO RUN IT WHILE DEVELOPING -- IMPORTANT
The install downloads roughly 785 MB (GHC wasm bindist 467 MB, wasi-sdk 187 MB, binaryen
65 MB, node 32 MB, wasm-tools 24 MB, cabal 9 MB) and then runs `./configure && make
install` on the GHC bindist. Expect 15-40 minutes wall clock. That EXCEEDS the 10-minute
maximum timeout of a foreground shell command in your tool harness. You must launch it as
a BACKGROUND command, tee its output to a log file under /tmp, and poll the log until it
finishes. Do not conclude it has failed because a foreground call timed out.

DONE LOOKS LIKE
- /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/install-toolchain.sh exists, is executable, and `bash -n` clean.
- You have actually RUN it to completion on this machine, so that $HOME/.ghc-wasm exists.
- `bash -c '. "$HOME/.ghc-wasm/env"; wasm32-wasi-ghc --numeric-version'` prints a 9.14.x
  version. Paste that exact version string into your final report.
- `scripts/install-toolchain.sh --check` exits 0 and prints the pin.
- Report the measured wall-clock install time and `du -sh $HOME/.ghc-wasm`.
Downstream tasks in wave 2 cannot start until this install has completed, so treat
finishing the install -- not merely writing the script -- as the deliverable.
acceptance_checks: scripts/install-toolchain.sh is executable, bash -n clean, and pins ghc-wasm-meta commit c75985a1b58fb0376eea9149ba5c7b933b3c7455 with FLAVOUR=9.14.

The script contains no `curl ... | sh` / `| bash` construct and downloads nothing from gitlab.haskell.org; the mirror is cloned with git and the checked-out HEAD is asserted against the pinned commit.
The script is idempotent: a second invocation without --force exits 0 without downloading, and --check reports installed status with no network access.
The toolchain is actually installed on this machine: sourcing $HOME/.ghc-wasm/env makes wasm32-wasi-ghc (9.14.x) and wasm32-wasi-cabal available.
$HOME/.ghc-wasm/.sxc1-toolchain-stamp records the pinned commit, flavour and resolved GHC version.
Preflight fails with a single clear message listing every missing prerequisite rather than dying midway through an install.

tasks.title: Static HTML/CSS shell, WASM boot loader, and vendored WASI browser shim
tasks.prompt: You are implementing one task of milestone M0 of the SXC-1 Trainer project. Repository root: /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1. You own exactly this directory and everything under it: /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/site/static/ Do not create or edit anything outside it. In particular another agent owns /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/site/app/, the .cabal files, and all of /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/. PINNED VERSIONS FOR MILESTONE M0 (do not substitute): ghc-wasm-meta github.com/haskell-wasm/ghc-wasm-meta @ c75985a1b58fb0376eea9149ba5c7b933b3c7455 GHC wasm FLAVOUR=9.14 (base 4.22.0.0, template-haskell 2.24.0.0, text 2.1.3, bytestring 0.12.2.0, containers 0.8, mtl 2.3.1, transformers 0.6.1.2, ghc-experimental 9.1401.0) miso 1.12.0.0 from Hackage, with index-state 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z WASI shim @bjorn3/browser_wasi_shim 0.3.0 toolchain root $HOME/.ghc-wasm (env script: $HOME/.ghc-wasm/env) WHAT THIS IS site/static/ is copied verbatim into the build output site/public/ by scripts/build-site.sh (written by another agent). The build then adds two generated files next to your files: `app.wasm` (the compiled Haskell app, a WASI *reactor* module) and `ghc_wasm_jsffi.js` (an ES module emitted by GHC's post-link step, whose default export is a function taking the instance-exports object and returning the `ghc_wasm_jsffi` import object). Miso's entire JavaScript runtime is embedded inside ghc_wasm_jsffi.js, so there is no separate miso.js to load. Your job is the HTML page and the loader that boots the module. SHARED BOOT / TEST CONTRACT (identical in every M0 task -- do not deviate): - window.__SXC1_BOOTED === true set by site/static/index.js after hs_start() resolves - window.__SXC1_BOOT_ERROR string; set instead if boot threw - #boot-status element visible before boot; hidden on success, shows the error text on failure - #counter-value element whose textContent is the model integer - #btn-increment / #btn-decrement / #btn-reset the three buttons Output directory served to browsers is site/public/ and contains, at its root: index.html index.js app.wasm ghc_wasm_jsffi.js .nojekyll vendor/browser_wasi_shim/ All URLs in index.html and index.js MUST be relative ("./app.wasm"), never root-absolute ("/app.wasm") and never an external origin -- the site must work when hosted at https://.github.io// and offline. FILES TO CREATE (1) site/static/.nojekyll -- empty file. Required so GitHub Pages does not filter paths. (2) site/static/vendor/browser_wasi_shim/ -- vendored copy of the WASI browser shim. Do NOT load it from a CDN. Fetch and verify: URL https://registry.npmjs.org/@bjorn3/browser_wasi_shim/-/browser_wasi_shim-0.3.0.tgz sha256 241c96716da84579e1045446f4f76faf637b97b1983ed7e9e590b71667a6c1b7 Abort if the checksum does not match. From the tarball copy into the vendor dir: package/dist/index.js wasi.js fd.js fs_mem.js fs_opfs.js strace.js wasi_defs.js debug.js (NOT tsconfig.tsbuildinfo) package/LICENSE-MIT package/LICENSE-APACHE These files import each other by relative path, so keep them in one flat directory. dist/index.js re-exports WASI, WASIProcExit, Fd, Inode, File, Directory, OpenFile, OpenDirectory, PreopenDirectory, ConsoleStdout, SyncOPFSFile, OpenSyncOPFSFile, strace. Also write site/static/vendor/browser_wasi_shim/VERSION.txt recording package name, version 0.3.0, the URL, the sha256, the licence ("MIT OR Apache-2.0") and today's date. Do not reformat or edit the vendored JS. (3) site/static/index.html -- a single self-contained page: - , lang="en", charset utf-8, - SXC-1 Trainer - An inline
verify_commands: bash -c 'for f in index.js wasi.js fd.js fs_mem.js fs_opfs.js strace.js wasi_defs.js debug.js LICENSE-MIT LICENSE-APACHE VERSION.txt; do test -f /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/site/static/vendor/browser_wasi_shim/$f || { echo missing $f; exit 1; }; done; echo vendor ok'

node --experimental-vm-modules -e "const fs=require('fs'),vm=require('vm'); new vm.SourceTextModule(fs.readFileSync('/home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/site/static/index.js','utf8')); console.log('index.js parses as ESM')"
acceptance_checks: site/static/ contains index.html, index.js, .nojekyll and vendor/browser_wasi_shim/ with all eight dist JS files plus both licence files and VERSION.txt.
The WASI shim is vendored from the npm tarball for version 0.3.0 with sha256 241c96716da84579e1045446f4f76faf637b97b1983ed7e9e590b71667a6c1b7 verified; nothing is loaded from a CDN at runtime.
index.html and index.js contain no external origin and no root-absolute URL, so the bundle works when hosted under a GitHub Pages project sub-path.

index.js instantiates ./app.wasm with wasi_snapshot_preview1 and ghc_wasm_jsffi imports, calls wasi.initialize(instance) before instance.exports.hs_start(), and sets window.__SXC1_BOOTED on success / window.__SXC1_BOOT_ERROR and a visible #boot-status message on failure.
All visual styling lives in index.html's inline <style>; the Haskell app contributes markup only.

tasks.title: Dependency-free headless-Chrome acceptance driver and static dev server
tasks.prompt:
You are implementing one task of milestone M0 of the SXC-1 Trainer project.
Repository root: /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1. You own exactly these two files:

    /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/browser-check.mjs
    /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/serve-site.sh

Do not create or edit any other file. Other agents own site/static/, site/app/ and the
other scripts/*.

PINNED VERSIONS FOR MILESTONE M0 (do not substitute):
  ghc-wasm-meta   github.com/haskell-wasm/ghc-wasm-meta @ c75985a1b58fb0376eea9149ba5c7b933b3c7455
  GHC wasm        FLAVOUR=9.14   (base 4.22.0.0, template-haskell 2.24.0.0, text 2.1.3,
                                  bytestring 0.12.2.0, containers 0.8, mtl 2.3.1,
                                  transformers 0.6.1.2, ghc-experimental 9.1401.0)
  miso            1.12.0.0 from Hackage, with index-state 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z
  WASI shim       @bjorn3/browser_wasi_shim 0.3.0
  toolchain root  $HOME/.ghc-wasm  (env script: $HOME/.ghc-wasm/env)

WHY THIS EXISTS
Milestone M0 is done when "a fresh clone builds with one documented command and produces a
working page in a browser". This task automates the browser half. Another agent's
scripts/check-site.sh will call your two files in wave 3; the Haskell app it tests does not
exist yet, which is why you must ship a self-test (below).

SHARED BOOT / TEST CONTRACT (identical in every M0 task -- do not deviate):
  - window.__SXC1_BOOTED === true      set by site/static/index.js after hs_start() resolves
  - window.__SXC1_BOOT_ERROR           string; set instead if boot threw
  - #boot-status                       element visible before boot; hidden on success,
                                       shows the error text on failure
  - #counter-value                     element whose textContent is the model integer
  - #btn-increment / #btn-decrement / #btn-reset   the three buttons
Output directory served to browsers is site/public/ and contains, at its root:
  index.html  index.js  app.wasm  ghc_wasm_jsffi.js  .nojekyll  vendor/browser_wasi_shim/
All URLs in index.html and index.js MUST be relative ("./app.wasm"), never root-absolute
("/app.wasm") and never an external origin -- the site must work when hosted at
https://<user>.github.io/<repo>/ and offline.

ENVIRONMENT FACTS (already verified on this machine -- rely on them)
  - Node v24.16.0 is on PATH and has a GLOBAL WebSocket class. Use it.
  - Google Chrome 151 is at /usr/bin/google-chrome (also google-chrome-stable).
  - Python 3.10 is on PATH and its mimetypes module maps .wasm to application/wasm, so
    `python3 -m http.server` is a valid host for WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming.
  - There is NO npm dependency budget: puppeteer, playwright, ws, jsdom etc. are all
    forbidden. Drive Chrome over the DevTools Protocol yourself using Node built-ins.

FILE 1: scripts/serve-site.sh
  bash, `set -euo pipefail`, executable. Serves a directory over plain HTTP on localhost.
    --dir  DIR   default: <repo>/site/public
    --port N     default: 8123   (env SXC1_PORT overrides the default)
    --help
  Resolve the repo root from BASH_SOURCE. Fail with a clear message if the directory does
  not exist ("run ./scripts/build-site.sh first"). Implementation:
      exec python3 -m http.server --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory "$DIR" "$PORT"
  Print the URL before exec'ing. Bind to 127.0.0.1 only, never 0.0.0.0.

FILE 2: scripts/browser-check.mjs
  A Node ES module (.mjs), executable, with a `#!/usr/bin/env node` shebang.
  Options:
    --url <url>       default http://127.0.0.1:8123/
    --browser <path>  default: $SXC1_BROWSER, else the first of google-chrome,
                      google-chrome-stable, chromium, chromium-browser found on PATH
    --timeout <ms>    default 45000 for the whole run
    --self-test       see below
    --keep-open       do not kill the browser on exit (debugging)
  Behaviour:
    1. Resolve the browser. If none is found, exit 2 with a message naming SXC1_BROWSER --
       this is a hard failure, not a silent skip.
    2. Launch it with a throwaway profile:
         --headless=new --disable-gpu --no-sandbox --no-first-run
         --no-default-browser-check --disable-dev-shm-usage
         --user-data-dir=<fresh mkdtemp> --remote-debugging-port=<free port> about:blank
       Pick the free port yourself by binding a net.Server to port 0 and closing it.
    3. Poll http://127.0.0.1:<port>/json/version (a few hundred ms apart, bounded by the
       timeout) until it returns JSON containing webSocketDebuggerUrl.
    4. Connect to that URL with the global WebSocket. Implement a tiny CDP client:
       monotonically increasing ids, a Map of pending promises resolved by matching id,
       and an event dispatcher for messages without an id. Support flat sessions:
       Target.createTarget({url:"about:blank"}) then
       Target.attachToTarget({targetId, flatten:true}) to get a sessionId, and include
       that sessionId on every page-scoped command.
    5. Enable Runtime and Page. Record every Runtime.consoleAPICalled with type "error"
       and every Runtime.exceptionThrown.
    6. Page.navigate to the URL, then poll Runtime.evaluate with awaitPromise until
       `window.__SXC1_BOOTED === true`. If `window.__SXC1_BOOT_ERROR` becomes a string
       first, fail immediately and print it -- that is the single most useful diagnostic
       this tool produces.
    7. Assertions, each printed as "ok"/"FAIL" with the observed value:
         a. #counter-value exists and its textContent trims to "0"
         b. after clicking #btn-increment, it reads "1"
         c. after two clicks of #btn-decrement, it reads "-1"
         d. after clicking #btn-reset, it reads "0"
         e. #boot-status is not visible (hidden, or offsetParent === null)
         f. zero console errors and zero uncaught exceptions were recorded
       Perform clicks with Runtime.evaluate calling document.querySelector(...).click(),
       and re-read the value after a short settle (poll for up to ~2s rather than a fixed
       sleep, so the test is not flaky on a slow machine).
    8. Always kill the browser and remove the temp profile (finally block, and on SIGINT).
    9. Print a summary. Exit 0 if every assertion passed, 1 if any failed, 2 on harness
       error (no browser, CDP unreachable, timeout).
  --self-test mode:
    Because the real app does not exist yet, --self-test must prove the driver works on
    its own. In this mode: create a temp directory, write an index.html into it that
    reproduces the contract with plain JavaScript (a counter with the same four ids, an
    initially visible #boot-status that it hides, and window.__SXC1_BOOTED = true), start
    `python3 -m http.server` on a free port serving that directory, run the identical
    assertion sequence against it, then tear everything down. Exit 0 only if all
    assertions passed. Do not weaken any assertion in self-test mode -- it must exercise
    the same code path as the real run.

  Write plain modern JS, no TypeScript, no build step. Comment the CDP plumbing.

DONE LOOKS LIKE
  - `node --check scripts/browser-check.mjs` is clean and `bash -n scripts/serve-site.sh` is clean.
  - `node scripts/browser-check.mjs --self-test` exits 0 and prints all six assertions
    passing. You must actually run it.
  - Deliberately break the fixture (e.g. make the increment button do nothing) and confirm
    the harness exits non-zero; state in your report that you did this. A checker that
    cannot fail is worthless.
  - No file under node_modules, no package.json, no npm install anywhere.
acceptance_checks: scripts/browser-check.mjs drives Google Chrome over the DevTools Protocol using only Node built-ins (global WebSocket, net, child_process, fs) -- no npm packages, no package.json, no node_modules anywhere in the repo.

`node scripts/browser-check.mjs --self-test` exits 0 and prints the same six assertions used against the real site (counter starts at 0, increment, two decrements, reset, boot-status hidden, no console errors/exceptions).
The harness fails loudly rather than skipping when no browser is found (exit 2 naming SXC1_BROWSER), and surfaces window.__SXC1_BOOT_ERROR verbatim when the WASM app fails to boot.
Assertions poll for a settled value with a bounded timeout instead of using fixed sleeps; the browser process and temp profile are cleaned up on every exit path.
scripts/serve-site.sh serves site/public over python3 -m http.server bound to 127.0.0.1 only, with --dir/--port/--help and a clear error when the directory is absent.
Negative control confirmed: the implementer broke the self-test fixture and observed a non-zero exit.

tasks.prompt:

PREREQUISITE ALREADY SATISFIED
The GHC WebAssembly toolchain is installed at $HOME/.ghc-wasm by
scripts/install-toolchain.sh. Activate it in any shell with `. "$HOME/.ghc-wasm/env"`,
which puts wasm32-wasi-ghc, wasm32-wasi-cabal, wasm-opt and wasm-tools on PATH.

  ghc-wasm-meta   github.com/haskell-wasm/ghc-wasm-meta @ c75985a1b58fb0376eea9149ba5c7b933b3c7455
  GHC wasm        FLAVOUR=9.14   (base 4.22.0.0, template-haskell 2.24.0.0, text 2.1.3,
                                  bytestring 0.12.2.0, containers 0.8, mtl 2.3.1,
                                  transformers 0.6.1.2, ghc-experimental 9.1401.0)
  miso            1.12.0.0 from Hackage, with index-state 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z
  WASI shim       @bjorn3/browser_wasi_shim 0.3.0
  toolchain root  $HOME/.ghc-wasm  (env script: $HOME/.ghc-wasm/env)

The whole miso dependency closure -- base, bytestring, containers, text, mtl,
transformers, template-haskell, ghc-experimental -- is already shipped as boot libraries in
the GHC 9.14 wasm bindist and every one of miso 1.12.0.0's version bounds is satisfied by
them. Only `miso` itself is compiled from source, so the build is minutes, not hours.

SHARED BOOT / TEST CONTRACT (identical in every M0 task -- do not deviate):
  - window.__SXC1_BOOTED === true      set by site/static/index.js after hs_start() resolves
  - window.__SXC1_BOOT_ERROR           string; set instead if boot threw
  - #boot-status                       element visible before boot; hidden on success,
                                       shows the error text on failure
  - #counter-value                     element whose textContent is the model integer
  - #btn-increment / #btn-decrement / #btn-reset   the three buttons
Output directory served to browsers is site/public/ and contains, at its root:
  index.html  index.js  app.wasm  ghc_wasm_jsffi.js  .nojekyll  vendor/browser_wasi_shim/
All URLs in index.html and index.js MUST be relative ("./app.wasm"), never root-absolute
("/app.wasm") and never an external origin -- the site must work when hosted at
https://<user>.github.io/<repo>/ and offline.

FILE 1: site/cabal.project

    packages: .

    index-state: 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z

    -- Use the boot libraries shipped inside the wasm32-wasi GHC bindist instead of letting
    -- the solver rebuild newer copies from Hackage for wasm32.
    constraints:
      base installed,
      ghc-prim installed,
      ghc-bignum installed,
      ghc-internal installed,
      ghc-experimental installed,
      ghc-boot-th installed,
      template-haskell installed,
      array installed,
      deepseq installed,
      bytestring installed,
      containers installed,
      text installed,
      mtl installed,
      transformers installed

    allow-newer:
      all:base,
      all:template-haskell

  If the solver reports that one of those constrained packages is not installed, delete
  only that single line and re-run; do not delete the whole stanza and do not add
  source-repository-package entries.

FILE 2: site/sxc1-trainer.cabal

    cabal-version:      3.0
    name:               sxc1-trainer
    version:            0.1.0.0
    synopsis:           SXC-1 Trainer - M0 toolchain spike
    build-type:         Simple

    common app-options
      if arch(wasm32)
        ghc-options: -no-hs-main -optl-mexec-model=reactor "-optl-Wl,--export=hs_start"
        cpp-options: -DWASM
      if arch(javascript)
        ld-options:  -sEXPORTED_RUNTIME_METHODS=HEAP8
        cpp-options: -DJS

    executable app
      import:           app-options
      main-is:          Main.hs
      hs-source-dirs:   app
      build-depends:    base < 5, miso == 1.12.0.0
      default-language: Haskell2010
      ghc-options:      -O1 -Wall -ferror-spans

  The executable MUST be named `app` (the build script and the loader depend on app.wasm).
  Keep the arch(javascript) stanza even though M0 does not build it: it is the project's
  documented fallback path and costs nothing now.
  The three wasm ghc-options are load-bearing: -no-hs-main suppresses the C main stub,
  -optl-mexec-model=reactor makes a library-style module with an _initialize export instead
  of a _start command, and --export=hs_start stops the linker's dead-code elimination from
  dropping the entry point. Copy the quoting of "-optl-Wl,--export=hs_start" exactly.

FILE 3: site/app/Main.hs -- a Miso 1.12 counter. Contribute markup ONLY; all styling is in
site/static/index.html. Verified-correct API for miso 1.12.0.0:
  startApp :: Eq model => Events -> App model action -> IO ()
  type App model action = Component ROOT () model action
  component :: model -> (action -> Effect ...) -> (props -> model -> View model action) -> Component ...
  type Effect parent props model action  -- a MonadState over model
  Miso.Lens supplies `this`, (.=), (+=), (-=); Miso.String supplies `ms`; Miso.Types
  supplies `text`. Miso.Html.Element has main_, h1_, p_, div_, output_, button_, span_.
  Miso.Html.Property has id_, class_. Miso.Html.Event has onClick.
  `View model action` has an IsString instance, so a bare string literal is a valid child.

    {-# LANGUAGE CPP               #-}
    {-# LANGUAGE LambdaCase        #-}
    {-# LANGUAGE OverloadedStrings #-}
    module Main (main) where

    import           Miso
    import           Miso.Html.Element  as H
    import           Miso.Html.Event    as E
    import           Miso.Html.Property as P
    import           Miso.Lens

    data Action = Increment | Decrement | Reset deriving (Show, Eq)

    #ifdef WASM
    foreign export javascript "hs_start" main :: IO ()
    #endif

    main :: IO ()
    main = startApp defaultEvents counterApp

    counterApp :: App Int Action
    counterApp = component 0 updateModel viewModel

    updateModel :: Action -> Effect parent props Int Action
    updateModel = \case
      Increment -> this += 1
      Decrement -> this -= 1
      Reset     -> this .= 0

    viewModel :: props -> Int -> View Int Action
    viewModel _ n = H.main_ [ P.id_ "app" ]
      [ H.h1_ [] [ "SXC-1 Trainer" ]
      , H.p_ [ P.class_ "subtitle" ] [ "M0 toolchain spike - Miso compiled to WebAssembly" ]
      , H.output_ [ P.id_ "counter-value" ] [ text (ms n) ]
      , H.div_ [ P.class_ "buttons" ]
        [ H.button_ [ P.id_ "btn-decrement", E.onClick Decrement ] [ "-" ]
        , H.button_ [ P.id_ "btn-reset",     E.onClick Reset     ] [ "reset" ]
        , H.button_ [ P.id_ "btn-increment", E.onClick Increment ] [ "+" ]
        ]
      ]

  Use element ids, not data-* attributes: miso's data_ helper goes through textProp, and
  miso.js only falls back to setAttribute for keys that are not DOM properties, whereas
  `id` always lands as a real attribute. Adjust the code above only as needed to compile
  against the real 1.12.0.0 API; keep every id and the -Wall-clean requirement.

FILE 4: site/.gitignore -- ignore `dist-newstyle/` and `public/`.

FILE 5: scripts/build-site.sh -- bash, `set -euo pipefail`, executable, resolves the repo
root from BASH_SOURCE, supports --help and --optimize.
    1. PREFIX="${GHC_WASM_PREFIX:-$HOME/.ghc-wasm}". If "$PREFIX/env" is missing, exit
       with "GHC WebAssembly toolchain not found - run ./scripts/install-toolchain.sh".
       Otherwise `. "$PREFIX/env"`.
    2. JOBS="${SXC1_JOBS:-2}". Do NOT use the toolchain's default of $ncpus: this machine
       has 4 cores but only ~3.9 GiB of usable RAM and 2 GiB of swap, and 4 parallel GHC
       processes risk the OOM killer. Document SXC1_JOBS=1 in the --help text.
    3. cd "$REPO_ROOT/site" and run: wasm32-wasi-cabal build -j"$JOBS" exe:app
       (No `cabal update`: the toolchain installer already updated the index, and the
       pinned index-state makes the resolution deterministic. Offer --update as a flag if
       you want an escape hatch.)
    4. WASM="$(wasm32-wasi-cabal list-bin exe:app | tail -n1)"; abort if it is not a file.
    5. rm -rf site/public; mkdir -p site/public; cp -R site/static/. site/public/
       (the trailing `/.` matters -- it copies .nojekyll too).
    6. Run the JSFFI post-link step BEFORE any stripping, because stripping removes the
       custom wasm section it reads:
         "$(wasm32-wasi-ghc --print-libdir)/post-link.mjs" --input "$WASM" \
             --output site/public/ghc_wasm_jsffi.js
    7. cp "$WASM" site/public/app.wasm   (copy under that exact name regardless of what
       list-bin returned).
    8. Only when --optimize was passed, and only if both tools resolve on PATH:
         wasm-opt -all -O2 site/public/app.wasm -o site/public/app.opt.wasm
         wasm-tools strip -o site/public/app.wasm site/public/app.opt.wasm
         rm -f site/public/app.opt.wasm
       Optimisation is OFF by default: binaryen is the one step that can silently
       miscompile GHC output, and M0's definition of done must not depend on it.
    9. Print a summary: resolved GHC version, wall-clock duration, and the byte size of
       app.wasm and ghc_wasm_jsffi.js (both raw and `gzip -c | wc -c`).

BUILD-TIME NOTES
  - A cold build downloads and compiles miso; run it as a BACKGROUND command with output
    teed to a log, because it can exceed the 10-minute foreground command timeout in your
    tool harness. Subsequent builds are fast.
  - If linking or compiling gets OOM-killed, retry with SXC1_JOBS=1.

DONE LOOKS LIKE
  - ./scripts/build-site.sh completes and site/public/ contains index.html, index.js,
    app.wasm, ghc_wasm_jsffi.js, .nojekyll and vendor/browser_wasi_shim/.
  - This one-liner prints a list containing hs_start, memory and _initialize:
      node -e "const fs=require('fs');const m=new WebAssembly.Module(fs.readFileSync('/home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/site/public/app.wasm'));console.log(WebAssembly.Module.exports(m).map(e=>e.name).filter(n=>['hs_start','memory','_initialize'].includes(n)).sort().join(','))"
  - The compile is -Wall clean (no warnings from app/Main.hs).
  - You have seen the page work: run `./scripts/serve-site.sh` (owned by another agent, it
    already exists) and `node scripts/browser-check.mjs` against it; report the result.
  - Report: GHC version, cold and warm build times, app.wasm size raw and gzipped, and the
    same figures with --optimize so the README can record the trade-off.
verify_commands: bash -c 'for f in index.html index.js app.wasm ghc_wasm_jsffi.js .nojekyll vendor/browser_wasi_shim/index.js; do test -f /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/site/public/$f || { echo missing $f; exit 1; }; done; echo output ok'

node -e "const fs=require('fs');const m=new WebAssembly.Module(fs.readFileSync('/home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/site/public/app.wasm'));const n=WebAssembly.Module.exports(m).map(e=>e.name);for(const k of ['hs_start','memory','_initialize']){if(!n.includes(k)){console.error('missing export '+k);process.exit(1)}}console.log('wasm exports ok')"
acceptance_checks: site/cabal.project pins index-state 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z and constrains the GHC boot libraries to `installed`; miso is taken from Hackage at exactly 1.12.0.0 with no source-repository-package stanza.

site/sxc1-trainer.cabal builds executable `app` with the wasm32 stanza -no-hs-main / -optl-mexec-model=reactor / --export=hs_start, and retains an arch(javascript) stanza for the documented fallback backend.

site/app/Main.hs is a Miso 1.12 counter that compiles -Wall clean, guards `foreign export javascript "hs_start"` behind #ifdef WASM, contributes markup only (no styling), and uses ids #counter-value, #btn-increment, #btn-decrement, #btn-reset inside #app.
scripts/build-site.sh runs end to end from a clean tree and produces site/public/ containing index.html, index.js, app.wasm, ghc_wasm_jsffi.js, .nojekyll and vendor/browser_wasi_shim/.
The produced app.wasm exports hs_start, memory and _initialize, proving the reactor and export linker flags took effect.
post-link.mjs runs before any wasm-opt/wasm-tools strip step; optimisation is opt-in behind --optimize and the build succeeds with it off.
The build defaults to 2 jobs (SXC1_JOBS overridable) rather than the toolchain's $ncpus default, and fails with an actionable message when $HOME/.ghc-wasm/env is absent.

tasks.title: End-to-end verification script, root README build story, and .gitignore
tasks.prompt:
You are implementing one task of milestone M0 of the SXC-1 Trainer project.
Repository root: /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1. You own exactly these three files:

    scripts/build-site.sh          builds site/public/ from site/app + site/static

Read PLAN.md at the repo root for project context and briefs/M0-plan.md for the design
rationale (versions, risks, the fallback) -- the README should be consistent with them.

PINNED VERSIONS FOR MILESTONE M0 (do not substitute):
  ghc-wasm-meta   github.com/haskell-wasm/ghc-wasm-meta @ c75985a1b58fb0376eea9149ba5c7b933b3c7455
  GHC wasm        FLAVOUR=9.14   (base 4.22.0.0, template-haskell 2.24.0.0, text 2.1.3,
                                  bytestring 0.12.2.0, containers 0.8, mtl 2.3.1,
                                  transformers 0.6.1.2, ghc-experimental 9.1401.0)
  miso            1.12.0.0 from Hackage, with index-state 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z
  WASI shim       @bjorn3/browser_wasi_shim 0.3.0
  toolchain root  $HOME/.ghc-wasm  (env script: $HOME/.ghc-wasm/env)


SHARED BOOT / TEST CONTRACT (identical in every M0 task -- do not deviate):
  - window.__SXC1_BOOTED === true      set by site/static/index.js after hs_start() resolves
  - window.__SXC1_BOOT_ERROR           string; set instead if boot threw

  - #counter-value                     element whose textContent is the model integer

Output directory served to browsers is site/public/ and contains, at its root:

("/app.wasm") and never an external origin -- the site must work when hosted at
https://<user>.github.io/<repo>/ and offline.

FILE 1: scripts/check-site.sh -- the single command that proves M0's definition of done.
bash, `set -euo pipefail`, executable, resolves the repo root from BASH_SOURCE.
Options: --help; --skip-browser (also honour SXC1_SKIP_BROWSER=1); --port N (default 8123,
env SXC1_PORT); --dir DIR (default <repo>/site/public).
It must NOT build -- it checks an existing build and tells the user to run
./scripts/build-site.sh if site/public is missing. Run every check, print one
"ok"/"FAIL" line each with the observed value, and exit non-zero if any failed (do not
abort on the first failure; a full report is more useful).

Checks, in order:
  1. Required files exist at the root of site/public: index.html, index.js, app.wasm,
     ghc_wasm_jsffi.js, .nojekyll, vendor/browser_wasi_shim/index.js.
  2. app.wasm begins with the 8 bytes 00 61 73 6d 01 00 00 00 (\0asm plus version 1).
  3. Using node (no npm packages), compile the module and assert
     WebAssembly.Module.exports contains hs_start, memory and _initialize. This is the
     direct proof that the reactor exec-model and --export linker flags took effect.
  4. ghc_wasm_jsffi.js exists, is larger than 1 KB, and contains a default export.
  5. site/public/index.html and site/public/index.js contain no root-absolute URL
     (src="/, href="/, from "/, fetch("/) and no external origin (no http:// or https://).
     These two invariants are what make the bundle deployable under a GitHub Pages project
     sub-path with no third-party runtime dependency.
  6. Report byte sizes of app.wasm and ghc_wasm_jsffi.js, raw and gzipped (informational,
     never a failure).
  7. Browser check, unless skipped: choose a free TCP port (default 8123; if busy, pick
     another), start scripts/serve-site.sh --dir <dir> --port <port> in the background,
     wait until the port answers, run
     `node scripts/browser-check.mjs --url http://127.0.0.1:<port>/`, capture its exit
     code, then kill the server in a trap that fires on every exit path (including
     SIGINT). Propagate a browser failure into the overall exit status. When skipped,
     print a conspicuous "SKIPPED" line, and exit non-zero if --skip-browser was NOT
     requested but no browser could be found.
  8. Final summary line: "check-site: N/M checks passed".

  Prove the script can fail: after it passes, overwrite site/public/app.wasm with garbage,
  confirm check-site.sh exits non-zero, then restore the real file by re-running
  ./scripts/build-site.sh. Say in your report that you did this.

FILE 2: README.md -- the fresh-clone build story. Keep it tight and accurate; every
command must be one you have actually run. Sections:
  - Title and one-paragraph description: interactive English-language training course for
    the Casio SXC-1 sampler; a Haskell/Miso application compiled to WebAssembly and served
    as static files; unofficial fan project, not affiliated with Casio.
  - Status: M0 (toolchain spike) - a counter page proving the build pipeline.
  - Prerequisites: Linux x86_64 (or aarch64-linux / macOS, which the toolchain also
    supports); git, curl, tar, xz, unzip, unzstd (zstd), jq, make, a C compiler, sed;

    about 12 GiB of free disk. No system-wide Haskell installation is needed or created --
    everything lands in $HOME/.ghc-wasm.
  - Build, as a copy-pasteable block:
        git clone <repo> && cd casio-sxc1
        ./scripts/install-toolchain.sh    # one time; ~785 MB download, 15-40 min
        ./scripts/build-site.sh           # -> site/public/
        ./scripts/check-site.sh           # structural checks + headless browser test
        ./scripts/serve-site.sh           # http://127.0.0.1:8123/
  - A "Pinned versions" table: ghc-wasm-meta commit c75985a1b58fb0376eea9149ba5c7b933b3c7455,
    FLAVOUR 9.14 (state the resolved GHC version you actually observed), miso 1.12.0.0
    from Hackage with index-state 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z, cabal-install 3.14.2.0,
    @bjorn3/browser_wasi_shim 0.3.0 (vendored).
  - "Why not the documented one-liner": the upstream install is
    `curl https://gitlab.haskell.org/.../bootstrap.sh | sh`, but gitlab.haskell.org sits
    behind an Anubis proof-of-work wall and returns an HTML challenge page (HTTP 200,
    text/html) to non-browser clients, so we clone the GitHub mirror at a pinned commit
    and never pipe downloads into a shell.
  - Repository layout: a short annotated tree (site/, scripts/, manuals/, translations/,
    briefs/, .github/workflows/).
  - How it works: five sentences on the pipeline -- wasm32-wasi-cabal builds a WASI reactor
    module; post-link.mjs extracts the ghc_wasm_jsffi custom section (which also carries
    Miso's own JS runtime, because miso.cabal declares js-sources for arch(wasm32)) into
    ghc_wasm_jsffi.js; site/static is copied over it; index.js instantiates the module with
    a vendored WASI shim and calls hs_start; everything is relative so it hosts at any path.
  - Deployment: GitHub Actions builds and uploads site/public as a Pages artifact; nothing

    pass --skip-browser; reinstall the toolchain -> ./scripts/install-toolchain.sh --force;

  - A one-line pointer to briefs/M0-plan.md for design rationale and the fallback plan.

tasks.title: GitHub Actions workflow: build, verify, and publish to GitHub Pages
tasks.prompt:
You are implementing one task of milestone M0 of the SXC-1 Trainer project.
Repository root: /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1. You own exactly one file (create the directories):

    /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/.github/workflows/site.yml

Do not create or edit any other file. Do not modify the scripts -- call them.

PINNED VERSIONS FOR MILESTONE M0 (do not substitute):
  ghc-wasm-meta   github.com/haskell-wasm/ghc-wasm-meta @ c75985a1b58fb0376eea9149ba5c7b933b3c7455
  GHC wasm        FLAVOUR=9.14   (base 4.22.0.0, template-haskell 2.24.0.0, text 2.1.3,
                                  bytestring 0.12.2.0, containers 0.8, mtl 2.3.1,
                                  transformers 0.6.1.2, ghc-experimental 9.1401.0)
  miso            1.12.0.0 from Hackage, with index-state 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z
  WASI shim       @bjorn3/browser_wasi_shim 0.3.0
  toolchain root  $HOME/.ghc-wasm  (env script: $HOME/.ghc-wasm/env)

CONTEXT
The project is a Haskell/Miso application compiled to WebAssembly and published as static
files on GitHub Pages. PLAN.md requires "tests runnable in CI and a build that works from a
fresh clone" for every milestone. These scripts already exist and are the entire build story:

    ./scripts/install-toolchain.sh   installs the pinned GHC wasm toolchain into $HOME/.ghc-wasm.
                                     Idempotent; `--check` exits 0 when already installed.
                                     Cold run: ~785 MB download, 15-40 minutes.
    ./scripts/build-site.sh          builds site/public/ (the deployable directory).
    ./scripts/check-site.sh          structural checks plus a headless-Chrome test driven
                                     by scripts/browser-check.mjs over the DevTools
                                     Protocol with zero npm dependencies. GitHub's
                                     ubuntu-latest image ships Google Chrome, so this runs
                                     for real in CI. Honours SXC1_SKIP_BROWSER=1.

IMPORTANT SITUATION: the repository has no GitHub remote yet -- the owner has not decided
on its name or visibility. So the build-and-verify job must be unconditional and useful
immediately, while the Pages deployment job must be inert until Pages is enabled.

WRITE .github/workflows/site.yml
  name: site
  Triggers: push to main, pull_request, and workflow_dispatch.
  permissions: contents: read, pages: write, id-token: write
  concurrency: group "pages", cancel-in-progress: false

  Job `build` on ubuntu-latest:
    1. actions/checkout@v7
    2. actions/cache@v6 with id `toolchain`, path `~/.ghc-wasm`, key
       ghc-wasm-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('scripts/install-toolchain.sh') }}
       (the installer file contains the pinned ghc-wasm-meta commit, so its hash is the
       correct cache key; add a matching restore-keys prefix).
    3. Run ./scripts/install-toolchain.sh only when the cache missed
       (if: steps.toolchain.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'). Give the step a generous
       timeout-minutes (60).
    4. actions/cache@v6 for `site/dist-newstyle`, keyed on
       hashFiles('site/cabal.project', 'site/sxc1-trainer.cabal', 'site/app/**') with a
       restore-keys prefix so incremental builds reuse object files.
    5. ./scripts/build-site.sh
    6. ./scripts/check-site.sh
    7. actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5 with path: site/public
    8. On failure, upload site/public and any build log as a normal debugging artifact
       (actions/upload-artifact@v4, if: failure(), continue-on-error: true).

  Job `deploy`:
    needs: build; if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: name github-pages, url ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    single step id `deployment` using actions/deploy-pages@v5.

  Rules:
    - Use only first-party actions/* -- no third-party actions.
    - Do not install Nix, ghcup, stack, or a system GHC. The toolchain script is the only
      installer.
    - Do not add npm/node setup steps: browser-check.mjs uses the runner's built-in Node
      and no packages.
    - Add a short comment above the deploy job noting it stays inert until GitHub Pages is
      enabled for the repository (PLAN.md open question 1).
    - Every `run:` step must invoke a script that exists at the path given; verify each
      path yourself with `ls` before finishing.

DONE LOOKS LIKE
  - .github/workflows/site.yml exists and parses as YAML
    (`python3 -c "import yaml,sys; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/site.yml'))"` --
    PyYAML 5.4.1 is installed on this machine).
  - Every script path it references exists and is executable.
  - The build job would work on a cold runner: checkout, cache, install, build, check,
    upload -- in that order, with no undeclared prerequisite.
  - You cannot run GitHub Actions locally; instead, in your report, walk through each step
    and state which local command you ran to confirm the equivalent behaviour works.
verify_commands: python3 -c "import yaml,sys; d=yaml.safe_load(open('/home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/.github/workflows/site.yml')); assert 'build' in d['jobs'] and 'deploy' in d['jobs'], 'missing jobs'; print('workflow parses; jobs:', list(d['jobs']))"

bash -c 'set -e; for s in scripts/install-toolchain.sh scripts/build-site.sh scripts/check-site.sh; do grep -q "$s" /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/.github/workflows/site.yml || { echo "workflow does not call $s"; exit 1; }; test -x /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/$s || { echo "$s not executable"; exit 1; }; done; echo "all referenced scripts present and executable"'
acceptance_checks: .github/workflows/site.yml is valid YAML with a `build` job and a `deploy` job, triggered on push to main, pull_request and workflow_dispatch.

The build job caches ~/.ghc-wasm keyed on hashFiles('scripts/install-toolchain.sh'), runs the installer only on a cache miss with a generous timeout, caches site/dist-newstyle, then runs scripts/build-site.sh and scripts/check-site.sh and uploads site/public via actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5.
The deploy job is gated on refs/heads/main and non-pull_request, uses the github-pages environment and actions/deploy-pages@v5, and carries a comment explaining it stays inert until Pages is enabled.
Only first-party actions/* are used; no Nix, ghcup, stack, system GHC or npm setup steps appear anywhere.
Every script path referenced by a run: step exists in the repository and is executable.
permissions (contents: read, pages: write, id-token: write) and a concurrency group are declared at the top level.
